Some insight into my trade taken today. Hope I figured out this forum software and it doesnt look like a pigeon scrawl.

Below is the eur/usd 4hr chart. The colour bands are supply above and demand below. The 2nd last candle from the far right edge is a close just above an R/S area. Given the candle was long and little retrace towards the end of its life, I considered it strong and worthy of consideration.

Looking at the top left of the chart there are two red arrows, and yes I know my graphic design skills are akin to the great masters of the art world, but I digress.

The two arrows show where two levels had supply removed, but were spiked. It is worth keeping this in mind for future reference when price returns close to these levels. Only price action closer in on the day will tell us if price will push through and then we take more data from the daily/weekly chart.

Next chart is the 30min. A black horizontal line with a red tick mark shows the S/R flip I mentioned earlier and this is a close up view. Note how price broke through, came back, rested the level and took off like a banshee. A clear sign big money was at work here. I hesitated a little before taking the trade long due to the time of day, it was after 3pm London time and who knows if the NY guys will run with this. The lower time frame gave me my entry and this is coming up in the next chart....but to finish off my comments on this chart.....The two red arrows indicate areas where I know price will react, and it did. First reaction was brief enough to pull out some weak hands and give some easy money to the pro's. The second and left most arrow is where price is currently dancing around and where my first take profit target was located. My final target is the upper dotted red line.

My stop is now at entry + the spread. So its a free trade from here on in and no way to loose unless I get a gap down. At this point I offer prayers to any gods that will listen and talk secretly to the lucky rabbits feet that adorn my office. Doesnt sound lucky for the local rabbit population though!

Note, a sense of humor is essential in reading my posts.

And finally a 5min chart showing the gory details. The horizontal black line is the S/R flip zone close up and the retest is clearly visible. Text book stuff but so easy to miss this if you are fixated on very low time frames. My entry was a few candles late after the S/R test, thats what talking on the phone does to your concentration.
Now this is some bad ass journal. Awesome work. Great trading and good sense of humor. Thank you Doctor. Bookmarked!

Here is a new chart on Brent crude. It is not an active trade, but a heads up on what to look for next week.

First a little history lesson about the lure of money. In early 2008 it was announced we were in recession, many said, nah, its just a temporary thing cos last year was a boom year just like the last few before. Sure enough in 2008 when the 4th quarter numbers were released we saw the first sign of a slow down, but most still said, nah!

Cast your eyes my friends on this monthly Brent chart. Note the two vertical blue lines. These indicate the entire year of 2007. You will see what is referred to as a parabolic curve in price, it forms a very steep and near vertical climb. These price moves are unsustainable and once they break, you'd better not be anywhere near it. It is obvious (now that has been pointed out) that even though we were in recession there was a massive effort to push oil prices higher for one last money grab. In the last month of 2007 you can see the sell off commence, and this was before the annual figures were made public. Now how could professional money know that the figures for 2007 would mean no more higher oil prices?.....you wont have to think very hard.

Next chart is also of the month but with a upper black line showing where price was capped, a middle blue line showing an important S/R area where on the left most part shows a decision to push price up, then price came back to it for one more hit where some greedy fingers got burned because price pushed through.....right down to a lower S/R line which is the origin of the entire move up. When price touched this line it reacts back up, but with little conviction at first. But where did it go?....right to the middle S/R line. Price stayed at this level for many months where sell orders were absorbed and when it broke, it blew right through resistance and didnt look back. It reached the upper price area where the historic sells were located and it then got lost for a long time before making another attempt to push back up. It once again hit the upper resistance, bounced off, hit the lower line (resistance) to get more buy orders and it now attempting to get back to where the last sells are in the little box. Its not looking good for the bulls on the monthly chart, but we are only half way through that candle so far.

The price structure is looking more and more chaotic and will be so until it breaks the upper or lower lines. Given we all accept we are in recession the likely path is down and lets look lower for some additional intelligence on where the money men are planning.

Onto the weekly. At the bottom is a fresh untested buy area. The ultimate target for this time frame. Look at the middle black S/R line. Price hits this at A, forms two impressive bearish engulfing candles and yes only manages to hit a small lower line which is allowing it take some buys from the arrow at B and it slowly winds up until it hits the resistance line again, pushes through and comes back just a little before the deal is sealed and off it goes, I put in a green tick to show the entry point.

Price continues to the upper black line which is taken from the monthly chart and therefore has major significance and contains sellers as can be seen way to the left of the chart. Price reacts as we expect but takes a long time to reach the previous resistance line where A is, but of course this is now support and price bounces off and is currently heading for the little box I have drawn on. Given we have hit the upper line and my text which says bye bye buyers, means there has already been an attempt to remove the potential for a push through. Look at the arrow and you will see right of it (cant get it pixel perfect on MT$) a bearish candle that tried to form as a bullish candle where it closed on its highs but with no body, the following candle and its partner tells me this is a decision point where price is off to the down side again.

The price now would have to break through the box/sellers and also the decision point in order to make it through the upper resistance line. Also price structure shows the buyers have been taken in as we go up, so no clean demand left below until the resistance line is touched. The near term move to me on this chart is bearish and a weekly candle close so far today says it will indeed be a bearish close and we failed to make it to the sellers box. There is nothing to say early next week there may be a spike into the box, but there is no push happening yet.

The daily is next up. The lower line is our S/R area and the blue line is a new but easy to find S/R area on the daily. Remembered what i mentioned about price failing to get into the sellers box?.....who would have guessed that the S/R area on the daily would have held back price, yet another reason for any bullish moves to be difficult from here and it would take a lot more ummph than what is seen on the chart. The 2nd last candle is a lower close and well towards the bottom on the previous days candle. Note arrow A where price tested its break of the resistance line and headed for the upper resistance line which is from way back. But interestingly at arrow B price blew right through resistance and didnt even come back for a second glance. A sign from the bigger time frames that the move up is over. If price fails to reach the sellers box and buyer shave no interest in coming due to over head resistance, this will eventually fall away. We do have room on the higher frames given the move in 2007 has had only half the value taken back.

And finally the 4hr chart and man am I getting tired from this.

Lower line is S/R from the daily and middle line is a 4hr S/R area and the blue top line comes from our higher time frames as we already saw. The lower and middle lines form a range where price bounces around, nothing interesting in there until we get a break and test. The test came where I have an arrow indicating the entry and the target was the upper blue line, who could have guessed it would go there?....that comment was a combination of sarcasim and quick wit.,,,not to mention a wink from my charming and debonair character....I digress.

The arrow to the upper right shows a gap in price not visible on the higher time frames. So this is the earliest sign of price looking to had back down. Ideally a spike into the sellers box would make me happier about the move. At present on the 1hr price is trying to push through an S/R level. I wont put that chart on cos its easy enough to see.

And there you have it boys n girls. A run down from the monthly to 4hr in glorious colour. A lot more detail could go into the explanations but I would be typing for a week!

My own thoughts as you can see are for a bearish move in Brent crude next week. But like all trades we have to wait for the ideal time to enter and if we have enough factors that show us very clearly that the pro money people are taking it south.

A quick heads up. I watched a 4 hr candle on Brent close with a lot of buying that turned a bearish candle bullish. The tail spiked demand and now on the 5min I see a move higher, a decision to not take the last sellers, but instead break above, come back to retest and now a gap higher. This could be the catalyst for getting the price into supply for next weeks sell off.

I will post a chart later when I get a few items off my desk and outta my mind.

Final two trades this week and the first is eurusd and the second is eurgbp.

The first chart is eurusd 4hr and the 2nd last candle engulfed and closed below an area of support which is an S/R area. Only the 4hr candle showed me this trade was worth taking and given London was not far from closing time, I targeted two profit areas, the lower one is shown on the chart and the first is not shown which I will show on lower time frame charts.

Next up is the 1hr and to the left of price on the 2nd last candle you can see a decision point where price blew through, this was also at the S/R area and the break was strong.

15min chart up next and this gets closer to my first target, it is the long bullish candle left of price and the pull back at its origin. It was 3pm London time and only 1hr left for the trading day and I was not blinkered into waiting for the ultimate goal. Take what money is offered cos you wont be asked twice, or rarely!

Last one up is the 5min chart. I took this just to show you how the decision point was broken and my entry was on the close of the green candle. Price moved so fast I was lucky to get a fill that far up on the large bullish candle, 2nd in from the right.

The trade was closed after the 15min pull back area caused a hold up and it was getting close to 4pm London time and decided to call it a day/week. +88 points for the day.

I am a little tired so do excuse my lack of comments and hollywood special fx graphics on the pics. That, plus all the dancing girls are rehearsing for next weeks charts

Final trade for the week. eurgbp.

First up the 4hr chart, note the setup is the same as the previous eurusd trade, a closed 4gr candle just under an S/R area and a strong full bodied candle.....hmm a glass of wine suddenly sounds nice.

1hr chart here and the small pull back was a reaction to a spike back at around 22:00, but the next candle opens strongly and momentum is now on my side, the longs from above are dumping like crazy, not to mention this too is bearish engulfing on a grand scale. All good reason to be in this.

Last chart is 15min and the little hiccup in price is a closer view on the reaction to the spike I mentioned. Another nice strong candle and my target just like the eurusd trade was for the ultimate level, but this too as you see is taken at 2pm local and not much time remaining before the close. The trade began to show me 3, 4 and then 5 tails on 5min candles at the red spike to the left and below price at the historical time of 14:30 (ish my eyes are shot now).

The trade was closed out at the red spike level and a good day was had.

Now that the markets are closed, tomorrow is your day of research to see whats setting up on the longer time frames for next week. One I see already is audusd at support.

Thats all from me, time to relax and unwind and allow my eyes to recover from LCD monitor over load.....and there are a few beers chilling which will very soon be chilling me.

Nicely done. I have just a couple of questions as I've noticed you are taking breakout trades without a visible stop loss on the charts.

Do you have a set of trading rules or are you all out discretionary?

How do you building your position size? Do you use a fixed risk based on the mental stop?

Also, do you take longer term swing positions off the daily and H4 or mainly intraday?

Cheers:)

My last two trades I dont see as breakout trades, they were taken after an area of interest was broken and proof shown the move was continuing. My view of a breakout trade is where a level is broken and you take it immediately on the break. I need more information as a false break is more common place than a break that keeps on going. Look back though some charts and see how many breaks took off without looking back, most dont. Its safer to look for a move back into the area where the break happened.

Rules remind me of a method or a system and these dont work in my opinion, but each to their own. I try and show principles that are based upon fact and are repeatable and proven over time ever since the trading markets began will you see how price reacts off of historic levels. A system, method or set of rules do not take into account how price goes back to an old area of interest and how it left the old area. All these are very important to the kind of trading style I show.

I do not use any indicator other than price itself. A candle body and its wick and tail all have importance to me, especially when they are in important areas.

My stops are not always shown on the charts and most are mental and putting a line on the screen is good enough for me. I want to keep the charts as clean as a I can so people can see whats going on and not look at all the stuff I got in the way of price structure and price action. Stops also subjective to the individual trader and you might feel comfortable with a wider stop than the next guy. You decide before you place the trade how much heat (loss) you are willing to take if the trade were to go bad, and you also place your stop either a hard fixed stop with your broker or a mental stop. All new traders are better prepared to use hard stops as discipline is not something everyone exercises equally.

The last two trades I took and posted charts of are both lower position size than I typically take. My reasons are two fold. The time of day was getting late and any move is unlikely to hit the ultimate target shown on my charts. I put the target on the chart so that it will concentrate your eye on where to look and the other important time frames are all shown for reference and how I go about finding those areas. The other reason is the trade is in a place where most day traders wont feel comfortable and many will say its trading within a range and this is not ideal, I agree. But my entry and reaaons for taking the trade were based on solid facts and my first target on both was hit. Taking such trades as these mean the risk reward is not as good as I prefer, but its profit and a relatively short term move to reach the target. I would not suggest anyone try trades like that until they get a few years of watching screens in real time.

If I had rules, one rule would have been dont trade in the middle of a range. Now you see why I dont have rules and your eye will eventually focus on where opportunities prop up.

If you use a mental stop you will need to watch the charts all the time and not be hesitant to close the trade when the line is hit and not wait and hope it will go back from the line. This is a good way to loose an account. On occasion I will use a fixed stop with my broker if the area has been spiked or tested multiple time already, there is nothing worse than getting taken out and see the trade go in the direction you had decided on. If you were to use a mental stop on a 1hr+ time frame where either supply or demand was present historically and the pro money decided...no, we are taking it the other way, thats when a mental stop will test your nerve. A hard stop there is safer and by all means scale into a position slowly as price action shows you there is no desire of price to not go where you think it will go.

Most of my trades are from 30 minutes in duration to a few hours in duration. I rarely take trades longer than a day in duration because the width of a stop loss and the time taken for the trade to end means I miss other more profitable trades on lower time frames, and there are tons of these to be had. One exception last year was a 8 month trade on the Aussie dollar, a nice earner and the pull backs didnt take me out and I stepped along with it.

My preference is to take trade signals off the 4hr and higher time frames where I see supply and demand about to be hit, then I drop down to lower time frames and look for trades in the direction given to me by the 4hr or daily etc. If the market is slow I will take trades off lower time frames down to the 5 min and grab anything from 15 to 30 points.

Hey Harry,

The number 1 area was a break of 1 hourly supply, price had no choice only go up into the next area of supply. A look at the one hour after you mark these areas will show you. Price made a second attempt to break 1 hourly supply or at least push deeper into the top, which is did with a spike and there was no clean supply for quite a ways up after that and price drifted back down and spiked old supply from the 15th at 11:00am, it reacted back up and closed with an engulfing candle.

This is the area you have circled on the right of you chart which you correctly pointed out is a rest of the break, but is also a 1 hour test of the old supply and given we also have a 4 hour candle close which hold more potential than all lower time frames, we need to look carefully that that, and this is where I took the signal from and got all the other information I need for the 1hr and lower.

Your analysis is good and my only comment is to ensure that you keep an eye on whats going on higher up. In the London session we have an 11am and 3pm 4 hour candle close and both need careful attention. Lower down you will often find the last few seconds of an hourly candle close is met with furious anger, watch them during London and be entertained. A 1 hr candle close is traded as much as a daily candle, and this is all big bucks that take action on both candles.

If nobody has said it before, only look for a candle close and do nothing while its forming.

I attached a chart of eur/usd 5 min just to give you a closer view of the action.

The two boxes are supply. There is what looks like a minor support and resistance zone. But if you plot the same line and go all the way out to the daily, you will see the same line was pinned to the point, highly significant and bring the time frames lower you will see it formed more and more of an important S/R flip.

Back to the 5 min chart again, the most current S and R are shown on the left and minor supply is below. I call it minor as it is close to the upper supply with respect to the time frame. One attempt is made to spike the supply and fails, we eventually hit supply and close at S...you could split hairs as to whether it closed above or below the pixel, but the 15min does show a strong candle and it spiked supply and closed at the top of the box, maybe a touch above it if I took more time to tweak the lines.

The decision to go higher was sealed now because supply was broken and price headed higher for the next area of supply where it again stalled and eventually pushed through. Timing was not good because London was closing around there and time to take money off the table and into your pocket.

I wouldnt take mid range trades like this unless you can spot what now should be obvious.

I have a new chart on the Dax30 coming up today and typing the details on the graphics at the moment.

A whole heap of time goes into producing these charts and I dont have time to proof read them as I would like. Please point out any erros/typos and I will fix them. While the instrument traded on these charts is a commodity it has no significance other than to show all financial markets and all time frames are traded off the same principles.

What we have here is a monthly chart of the Dax30 index.

The horizontal blue lines are areas of major support, resistance, supply and demand and in some cases the areas where the market made a decided about face.

Starting on the left we have our blue line showing the upper end of a price consolidation area and the bottom line is now visible and is below the screen. Price pushed up through the blue where a decision was made, price returned to the line where resistance is now support and this also brings us to an important principle. When such a decision is made and resistance becomes support, it also tells us what was old supply becomes new demand, thus we have a new demand area. Many many traders miss this entirely. In fact in my previous post where I replied to a trade I took on the eur/usd last Friday, you can see the same thing happening on a lower time frame. Where you must place more importance to your trading decisions, it must be from the monthly time frame and lower. The first break we have here happened and the entry as shows where I have 'S' for support would have been taken at its close.

Those who use indicators would wait much longer for confirmation, and confirmation will take much profit from a move. You are getting into trades that no books or courses will tell you about. These areas we look for are not obvious and your eye and brain will take a while to see what is going on.

We have our entry and price moves up, and now I have a question for you all. In box A, what do all those green candles tell you?.....I will answer this later in the week. Think hard, the answer is not obvious at first.

My data feed only goes back to the early 1990's and I cant say why price stopped at the R above box A. But for the sake of education lets say its an old resistance area, and we mark the area with an R to show it is resistance over head. After box A price made a parabolic move up, terminated with a candle that has a long wick. This most of you will call rejection of higher prices, this is only partially correct. What it should also tell you is that in order for such a long wick to appear it means serious selling was taking place, and taking place right into retail buyers who were buying at the top where they felt comfortable buying and they had the 'confirmation' thing going on as the books will tell you. All lies!

Who do you think were the sellers up there?.....yes, the people I call pro money, professional money. And I dont consider pension funds and small banks i.e regional to be pro money. We know otherwise and know there is over head resistance and there has just been a parabolic move into resistance so the likely outcome is a sell off. And indeed the sell comes and it heads for where price wants to go, which is back into old demand and the origin of the move where I have the tick, jez, who would have guessed!

I wont labour the chart too much and will press on to box B. I now have the same question as box A. What do all those red candles tell you?

The answer I will give you is something I doubt anyone here will know and you wont find it in any books and you wont hear it mentioned at expensive trading courses. But it will make you think differently to the herd i.e retail trader.

Onwards...

Now we have hit the origin on the move past box B and we reach support. Another decision is made here in the green candle with tiny body not to bounce off, we then push through strongly and two attempts were made to reach the overall origin of the move up, but we do get there and end with a nice lot of buying into very old demand. We get a close above support and there is plenty evidence even for the most skeptic to go long. A second chance was given on the seond green candle where it showed a fake bearish move, but given we know for fact we are in monthly demand we would hold tough for at least the next resistance above, which is formed from two red pins and the decision point. Another 'who would have thought it would happen in there moment'.

Price breaks through resistance, comes back to test it, and now resistance becomes support and the supply we also just broke becomes......yep, new demand, a new area to look for in the future. We break easily break through the consolidation to our left because we know price has to move up from there to at least the next area of resistance or supply. We get a hiccup at old supply at the top of box B, but push even higher where the next target is....yes more old supply or resistance. In fact we hit both, and we being sensible traders take full profits due to hitting resistance, and supply and weak price action. Price falls back onto the top of old supply which now forms support. Look carefully at the X. What do you see?.....for most traders this is a pull back within a large range from the overall high on the top left, to the first test of the low where I have an S. The two candles form a valid setup for a long trade due to the fact that major buying is visible where the tails formed, plus it happens at support and at old supply which we now know becomes new demand. Nice huh?

Do I paint a picture in your mind yet?....this is not complex material to soak in. Trading is not complex.

Ok, now we are at support so price once again heads up look for more supply to take it back down. We push through the resistance and old supply that kept us down for a while, now the path is only one way, up. Given the price action left of where we now are, we do see very strong large bodied candles which means price will hit hard the top of old supply, which it does and in fact tried twice to push even higher. At this stage we are at historic highs. I would not take this higher at this point for all the tea in China. I will skip onwards a little to save some of you from total brain over load.

Price eventual works down to the box where I have text below it stating......1st higher high, heads up! What this signifies is on the monthly chart we now have a higher low and a sign price is unlikely to come back to this low for a long time. We also happen to hit on an old resistance area which again acted as support and where major buying came in because it is also a fresh and untested area. Also note the line I have on the bottom of the candle body close prices. Both are equal, but the tail is where the deal was sealed. That help hit support perfectly.

Skipping to the end as I am sure you will by now be able to read the chart on your own, the last three candles tells us we are looking into strong buying. The 3rd last candle closed above support, its tail not only spiked support but it also took all the buyers with it when it went deep into the last place where buyers came in. The other two candles done the same thing by taking the buyers with it, this can only mean we will likely go higher and the last candle while not yet fully formed suggests from lower time frame action we will see supply to the left ignored and we push into at least the supply in the very top box. After all, when you look for new fresh supply to the left, how far back to do have to look?.....The very top box. Another 'who would have thought' moment.

Weekly chart next up.

The two blue lines from the monthly are retained and have not be adjusted to clean them up and get a more accurate picture, but you should. This is just me working quickly on a Sunday. By now you know S means support and R means resistance. Look at the top two arrows, both show attempts to take out supply quickly, given both look like rather weak efforts I doubt they will be valid, but time will tell.

I have a thin black horizontal line where A and B show what most traders will say is mid range, which is is in the greater scheme of things. A is also resistance from price consolidation to its left. Remember, resistance when broken becomes support and when supply is broken is becomes demand. The opposite applies when come down, you can work that part out yourself.

Look at arrow A. It is a red candle with tiny body and long tail and closes at the high of the previous green candle. Of significance is this happens also on the monthly close candle, major buying here but not a trade that can be taken off the weekly. Where the candles form, how they close and the time frame they represent is the key. Higher time frame signals are powerful and you counter trend them at your peril on lower time frames and always keeping in mind this this can turn and bite you hard.

When you see the setup as I mentioned, look for the obvious signs, is pro money buying or selling? They cant hide billions of dollars for very long and it is unfortunate trading books and many forums all say that tails are rejection of lower price and wicks are rejection of higher price. That is only half the picture and it programs your brain incorrectly, it more importantly should state tails are buyers and wicks are sellers. It couples into price action nicely too and this is where I know a lot of people are getting confused because it means a bear candle is now suddenly a bull candle and a bull candle is a bear candle.

I have heard many are curious about the Doctor. There is much I cannot say, but of what I can say I will offer you this.

If there was a trading book I have not read, it has not been written. Virtually all books once forensically examined (as I have done) and the message in the text put into practice, it shows you where the book steers you in the wrong direction. Proving this is a simple matter but very time consuming because it takes a lot of testing on historic price and on many time frames. The same applies to DVD systems, methods, indicators and seminars. Please dont waste your money on those. The print and TV media is full of cleverly worded statements to push you along into making a decision, usually the wrong one. Contrary to a certain business TV channel's adverts, I do not know any traders who manage their money on the basis of what the TV channel says, all their news is old news, too late then.

Also consider some of the most basic phrases which are thrown around since the early 1900's.

The trend is your friend.......in order for a trend to be in place you must have two points where your trend line is drawn, all sounds good to most. But to form a trend you need for example in an up trend two higher highs and two higher lows. If you wait for that type of trend analysis you miss most of the move, try it on historic data and you will see how much profit is lost. Do you think there is any advantage in professional money telling you how they take a trade?....of course not!

Here is another classic. Buy dips in rallies....yeah sure, we missed the start of the move and now you want us to buy when there is clearly no target and no way of knowing where the move may end, eventually all dips turn into bearish moves. A real smart way to loose money.

Here is why Box A are sellers and Box B are buyers.

My hint earlier was where this is counter intuitive. The trading books, courses and media all steer you into trading in a herd like mentality and my answer to you know will at first sound wrong. Engage the logical part of your brain and see how the sense in this shows itself to you.

When you enter the market in Box A, you 'buy' into the market. You do not make any money until you close your position in profit, and profits are not gained unless there is a willing buyer of your position when you close it. He buys from you, (price is still going up) but your position is sold to him, therefore its a sell. Before you enter the market you must ask yourself some simple questions.

If I enter at price x, who am I likely buying from and who am I likely trading alongside. Is it the right place and I am not buying blind or where there is high volume. All moves by professional money begin when there is little volume, they slowly filter orders into the market so that the large amount of money they have to trade (orders) will not cause price to move much from where it is now. Remember, even a few points the wrong way is critical for them and hurts profitability and can tie up funds too long for intraday trades.

Assuming you picked your entry price and you place an order and now you get a fill.

Now what?

You were a buyer, now you are a seller. Another question you ask is, where do I exit with profit? (price level) You identify your exit before you place your order and also your stop. Counter intuitive is allowing yourself to think ahead where you must get out, and this is best done into the willingness of weak hands who all jump at the market when its moving hard in case they miss the move. They always buying at the top, right where your target is and they 'buy' your 'sell' (close position) which on the most common forex trading platform MT4 is called 'close'.

The Box B is the inverse of this.

It gels with the concept of buying when prices are low and selling when prices are high and where most wont see why the price at those areas is where you should be placing a trade. But nothing is earned unless the trade is completed in profit and at the right place. If you dont get a fill when you wish to close, you get slippage, requotes etc. This all points to a narrow price range where there is a great deal of activity.

There is some insight into how all this works behind the scenes. Any sign of slow processing of orders mean there is a large volume of trading going on at the level. You will also see spreads widen because the broker does not want you to get away totally with the upper hand. Those guys always get their profit from you.

Does this make sense to you yet?

Think of you being in the minority of traders (the successful ones) when entering the market and getting out when the herd are still willing to buy, you must see from their perspective what you no longer look for i,e buy dips on rallys, head and shoulder neck break, double top etc etc. Knowing where the herd will probably place a trade that fits perfectly with your exit is essential, trade toward them when they will be happy to take your order when you close it.

i was recently asked to look over a topic in the school room part of the forum and rather than push the posters thread in a new direction, I decided to put some digital ink here and help you make sense of what order flow is and how it works.

The London close and any other session close is of no significance in the greater scheme of things. What most of you see will typically break down into two common moves, the next session will reverse the previous session, or it will work price to where the next batch of major orders lay. Many times London will close with lots of positioning going on. Some of you will see positioning as the term compression. But it has no defined shape or pattern, it is simply a slow price grind to an entry price area.

Never forget the fundamentals behind price movement, it will only break in the direction where more orders have been placed and the break will leave pending orders behind at the breaking price and these price levels are future targets on all time frames. The higher time frames give the greatest reaction as more of the professional money will be targeting those. Intraday targets are less dramatic in movement unless they happen upon a 4hr+ area of old movement. We know there will always be pending orders remaining to be filled at those now old prices, because the banks and institutions will have been given instructions from their customers to sell currency x and a particular price. The banks and institutions cannot get all the orders into the market at the desired price because it will cause the price to move too far from the desired order price.

Asia tends to have a subdued trading session and only when the EU and London sessions get under way will you get movement, the majority of the worlds money is traded in the London session and a great deal of the good moves happen in that session.

it is better if you dont beat yourself up looking for some secret to any session in particular, because there are no secrets to trading, no special or hidden signals. It is all plain Jane and in your face if you constantly refer to the big picture i.e higher time frame and then drop down for a closer view. I see too many people trying to conduct an of over analysis of what is very simple in reality. There are no banks or institutions that know what way price will break, they know as much as we do and its all right there on the charts. They look for the same things we do and their only edge, and it is a very slight edge, is the bigger players will have custom orders that tell them where their customers want to deal. In the overall picture this information has little validity because it can only be proven accurate after a move. Therefore historical price now becomes an asset to them and all other traders once they know where to look. This is what we do here in case the penny has not yet dropped.

There is also talk going on in this forum about liquidity and there is a very obvious fact which is easily over looked. Books and those who quote from them often state price can only do one of three things, price goes up, price goes down, and price goes sideways. Nonsense!

Price cannot go sideways, price is not a vector and can only rise or fall.

Order flow in the market determines how long it takes for price to move with more vigor than it does when in a period of consolidation. The amount of money traded to make any move happen is not a set amount or even a minimum amount of orders, in the end price will only move where there are more orders placed of a particular type i.e long or short. Nobody knows how many orders of each type there are in the forex market, there is no central exchange and no way to get the order information. Dont waste your time trying to find a way, countless others before you tried ways and all failed.

When price moves, those who were wrong are stopped out, new orders come in from those who are reversing their position and retail traders jump in as price is moving and those who were first stopped out also add momentum to the move with market orders in the direction of the break, mainly retail traders.

All we can do at best is look for historical reasons and apply this to a level or price area for possible future moves. Trading is neither science or art, it is a reflection of what value humans place on a particular financial instrument at a given point in time.

Patience, take your time and let your brain soak in the charts. Screen time is your friend.

The longer time frames are where the money comes in and once you drop down lower, look for the small areas where you see the first one of two pull backs, this will form support or resistance for the main move. Lets really get into the details now.

Here is a zoomed in view of the last leg down in price. To help guide your eye here, candle 1 was a race to grab old demand and is also taken at support.

2 the bulls have already got their work done and the follow through buy intraday bears is weak the close well off the lows.

3 the bulls intent is obvious here with a very large body and close with very little wick on top. On the other chart you will see this candle hit old supply.

4 considering we just hit old supply this candle close showed such weak bullish momentum that it was plain to see we need to fall back down, or collect more orders to break above.

5 a weak bearish candle, note how it closed well inside the previous candles low, note the long tail, a sign of buying.

6 a very strong bull candle with strong close above support, so we long this puppy to the moon now right?

7 no, we wait for a pull back and see does support hold. And 7 is a perfect bearish engulfing candle and proves candle 6 was a false bullish break.

8 unfortunately the market timing for the previous move was not very good and we are now stuck between close in old supply and demand. When this happens we need to keep the big picture in mind, we are still below supply. This candle attempts to grab more orders from the bulls by the tail showing buying, however the weak close tells is its going nowhere.

9 we have a break below near term candle 5 and old demand from candle 3. But hitting candle 3's demand hard means we have to see a reaction higher.

10 this is the reaction from candle 9, it has setup up pro money for the main bearish move.

11 this is interesting, the candle pushed lower than the previous candles wick and closed within the body of candle 3 which is still the most significant candle we need to break.

12 finally a strong break and strong close. Of note here is the candle got into the tail of candle 1. There were a lot of buyers here and even though it is not the first time price has been in that area, there is validity given to this area given its likely hood to act as resistance once broken and retested.

13 no interest in taking price lower yet and no progress made by bulls or bears. The very slight tail below the tiny body means we wait.

14 this is the start of the pro bears selling. See how the wick pulls in supply from candle 12 and closes as a bullish looking candle but with a very low close on the candle 12 body. Books will tell you this is a bullish engulfing candle because it had contained the previous candle, correct, but, the books fail to tell you the reason for the wick and where it went.

15 Something to look at on this candle is the fact that the body is both bearish and closed within the previous candle, but no takers higher considering candle 14 is what is considered bullish. Pro money know better.

16 This is the bug push to get the market running and all the work prior to this candle was done in candle 14 and a lot of bears waited for this move whereas candle 14 would have got day traders long and now candle 16 would have stopped them out adding fuel to the bearish orders. 'A' shows where pro money have done their restest to see will the bears come in and if not, give the bulls another place to enter long with a safer margin for profit. Close of A was the entry long.

Above the purple line is a black line, this is placed at the origin of the sellers where I also indicated it wont be respected....eventually, how long we spend in that price area will say a lot for the move. Where you need to turn your brain upside down is that we are no longer bearish, but bullish and old supply is no longer valid to us on this chart and our primary lead comes off the higher time frame and watch how it helps setup new demand on this chart.

Above the black line is a 'D'. This is a decision to take price down further. It was so close to higher time frame demand that shorting there was not an option. It is from this old supply area where the major change in the market will come about. Once the new bullish order becomes established the additional newly created demand further up the chart and on lower time frames will become more reliable as pro money are happy to hold through all the daily pull backs.

The next black line up is very obvious S/R, w will expect a reaction from price up into this area and we once again look for price action to tell us how strong the market is. At that point we will start taking out a lot more of the long term bearish stops. There are longer term traders who do hold for too long and get taken out.

Finally on the very top we have three old supply areas all of which will become areas to watch for as price approaches. Getting the right order flow prior to these areas will mean a push through immediately. The timing needs to be correct for each move or it will allow price fall back down until it reaches support and where prices will be cheaper for the bulls to take in more long orders as the weak bulls bail out. There will also be further orders develop as price climbs and the new comer bears get stopped out. All this adds fuel to the continuing move up.

The transitional areas when day traders forget about the monthly and weekly is where most get chopped up badly and all could have been avoided if the bigger picture is examined each day. Even though this is a weekly chart and most here dont have the capital to trade this kind of move, you can still achieve the approx 230 point move from candle A to where price is now, by dropping down to a 5min and placing fractional lots. In fact scaling in like this on longer term moves is how I work my way through the daily chart and will keep putting in small lot sizes are prices moves. At worst I will loose the last order placed and get profit on all the previous trades. Look at my euro trade for all the trades placed and one of those is in excess of 230 points shown here and all my combined orders are several thousand points already and when the trade is closed it might break 10,000 points with all orders total, price action next week will tell me when to close some, or all. The idea is to reduce risk and hold through the deeper pull backs to realise the profit. Its still a lower risk means of getting larger profits without placing large lot trades in one or two places.

An example would be, if I were taking a day trade off the 5min for a typical move in one day and I liked the area I was placing the trade. I might put on between 2 and 10 lots. If the same 5min entry was to be used for a longer term hold, I will reduce down to.5 to 2 lots per trade and scale in as the subsequent entries come around. But each new entry will have the previous orders safe with stop above and in a safe place against normal price action and profit in the bank. My risk is now lower than placing large lots in one or two places and profit margin much higher than day trading.

The point I want to drive home is to never be fixated on the market is bullish or bearish and learn to recognise the high time frame supply and demand turns. If they look choppy lower down, just wait for a few days and price action will start to look much cleaner.

There is so much noise on the internet and opinions offered that it is easy for anyone to get confused and jump from one thing to the next. The best advice I can offer anyone in trading new or old, is keep your charts ultra clean with no indicators, only horizontal lines (fewer is better) and only trade off a closed candle.

Just because there is a large candle, or large spike doesnt mean the market is changing direction or that it has to be like this because NY or London has closed. Price will move according to the direction given on higher time frames, because the real market movers operate only up that high and a daily spike of 100 points or more is meaningless unless its reach their new entry point, or exit point. Make sense?

Another basic and simple fact to keep in mind is at any market open or close is, if you are not in the market, wait and allow it settle. If you are already and want out, want for it to settle, false moves are very common around those times. If you find yourself getting stopped out, where was your stop and is there a trend in getting stopped out you can see?....there is always a reason. You can also scale in and out of trades to spread your risk thinner. This works well when you want to hold for longer periods of time. Loose the pivot points if you can and concentrate on price levels. Look for multiple reasons to take any trade, all must be obvious and pro money must show signs of activity for lower time frame entries to work.

The time frame you choose to enter must gel with your risk appetite and capital. Also be aware that when trading intraday you do not have the luxury of time. Where you place your entries, exits and how you manage the trades is a personal thing and there is no right or wrong, it is done to suit your pocket and style as a trader. Try developing a trading style on a time frame you feel comfortable with and take it from there. It will evolve over time into something that feels comfortable, and once you reach that, stop changing it and hone it down to become second nature. It has been a while since I posted a trade, so here is a live one. This is Brent crude on the daily time frame.

Overhead we have a gray box that is an old supply area, we touched the bottom of this box four days ago and I waited for a deeper push into the box. Clearly we didnt get a deeper push in and I had to sit and wait for the next area to be hit lower down and where some S/R and price action would bring a trade.

If you look at candle A, you will see it pinned old supply and the market rose as expected. But what does the close of that candle tell you?....look at its close in context to what history is around it, it is at the same price as the previous bullish move up. Pure fluke you say, yeah sure!

The following day we see a false bullish move which on the intraday charts would have had day traders going long. I had no intention of going long when pro money had already signaled their intentions. It was the break of the 2nd last candle today that got me in short. The entry was taken off the 15min chart as it tends to be a little easier to get entries with oil, rather than the 5min which can easily mess you about. If you look at your own 4hr chart you will see a large spike down, this was the candle that got my attention, note it pinned old supply. On the 1hr the same area has two candles with long tails and no bullish follow through, if you saw that and went long. Bad move, it was not a supply demand play at all. The overall market picture must be in your mind at all times and not focus purely on supply and demand intra day. The higher time frame price action and their supply and demand areas take priority.

Walking down from where I entered I have a number of choices for a target. I can go for the last demand area which is pretty much hit now, or go lower to my blue line which is the most significant S/R on the chart and an obvious place as I like to see. Or I can sit through the pain of the ugly decision area which is a real messy price action area, but if broken there is only place left to go ad that is 90usd or less. Do keep in mind my blue S/R line did see strong bullish move off back in Dec 2011. A reaction there is highly likely, but equally likely not to turn the market back above 118 unless the bulls manage to get a ton of orders.

There is the possibility we are at the beginning of a bear oil market. We need a lot more information before taking longer term bearish trades. A few weeks of bearish price action would suit my view of the market, then wait for weekly and monthly candles to tell us more. If you played this move intra day, it is now over. And you wait again.

Simon, the odd good book is out there and the best info is gleaned from reading up on candle sticks rather than a trading method or system. In time all successful traders develop a style that is unique to them. This is not a one fits all type deal, and given we individuals, we will also learn as an individual and create our own individual style and techniques. Dont take my info here as the be all and end all because it is not.

A good candle book is Steve Nisson's work. Learning a candle stick on its own is easy and anyone can do it. Learning them in context is where all the books and courses fall over because there are multiple times, time of day, beginning of month/week/day, news, gov statements etc all in the mix that will not gel with the classic description of what candle 'x' is meant to tell you.

Only screen time and regular analysis of price action will help make sense of price movement through the candle stick formations and where they fall within the large over all picture. But for a guy who only started this last year, your doing well.

Aaron, studying price action is best done with screen time. Get to recognise real price movement from noise and the intraday positioning that creates much of the chaotic looking price around some levels of interest. In time you will be able to get in much closer and see whats going on, but for now maintain a relatively broad outlook to keep some sensible direction in your head.

As you improve on the higher time frames, drop down a time frame and continue this as you improve. Given enough time you should be able to pick trades off any time frame and be right more times than wrong.

Simon, I dont think there any candle stick books that show candle sticks as they approach and leave areas of supply and demand. Most of the text will be candles alone, and then candles in context, but not in the context of supply and demand. Have you ever noticed how the majority of traders get excited with a pin bar which is really called a hanging man, or a reverse pin bar which is a shooting star?...same goes with a doji. They mean little to us unless they form in the right place because we want to be in the move before all the retail traders where the various schools of though with moving averages must cross, or a pull into a certain value moving average. I want to take money from retail traders because I cant take it from the pro's. Good fortune means this tends to work the vast majority of the time:)

The most useful thing to do first is get the accepted meaning of a candle in your head first and then look at historic supply and demand areas and look for candle sticks that make sense of the move into and out of the area.

There are no set patterns or formations because the market will not show the same path twice. In time you will find some common things to look for and then build around those where some subtle signs come in. All that has to be done with the higher time frames in mind and watch as they give signals for their supply and demand areas. The market has may faces and wont show the same one very often, pro money want to hide what they are doing for as long as possible, or at least until they filter in as many orders they possibly can. After that, all it takes is one little push and off it goes.

This is a 5min chart and not to be taken as trading advice or a reason to place a trade. What I want to show you here is how a market direction changes and what signs to look for. There is no 100% certainty that the market is changing now, but rather what signs tend to show up and what gives us reason to pay attention.

First off the blue line is support and resistance. I omitted by typical S/R comment as I see a lot of new people in here and its helpful to new people to get to terms with the buzz words us old farts throw around and not considering there are others who look at the screen and say....what?

Note the bullish break from the support line which is one of the most powerful things you can look for in trading. If you take longs off support and shorts off resistance you will do yourself a huge favor. What ties nicely into that is when support forms along side historic buying and resistance forming along side historic selling. Either one is a powerful combination and I have depended on this proven fact for a long time. Master one, then the other.

enough waffle, onto more charting. The bullish move off support has reached 4hr supply and we expect some reaction given it is the first test of this price area. What you cannot tell for sure is if there is enough reason for pro money to push up through old supply and absorb all the sellers, or just satisfy themselves they have enough profit to the long side and unwind their positions and look for the next move. Market timing for intraday trading like this is crucial for you to understand how it works. If you see a nice setup and its close to the market close, let it go. You only want to trade in an active market where pro money is also active.

Now that the 4hjr supply has been hit and the 4hr candle has closed on it lows, this is a good indication for further bearish activity, tomorrow, not now. You dont have the capital to trade this over night and have such a wide stop that any market spikes wont take you out. Make good use of your capital by trading it wisely and putting it to best use where you get profit within a reasonable period of time.

As price came back down it bounced off our blue line, pure price action. The move back up went nowhere and a sign of the bulls are about done. When price came down to the support line again, it blew right through and didnt look back for a long time. When it eventually came back it bounced back down proving to us that this area is an area of historic support and resistance and its giving us a trade entry....at some point in the future, or now if you have a trade plan in mind that works this early in.

A little more recent we got another small move up to the S/R line and off we bounce again.

Look at other time frames and note as price moved up all the little pull backs you see are a combination of profit taking and new orders, and the small fish bailing out. Always keep the over all market direction and its timing in the front of your mind so that you can at least recognise where the likely true reactions will be and not get suckered by all the low time frame noise and fake moves.

Tomorrow is Friday and a good day for a sell off. We have more room for margin/profit to the bearish side than we do for any bullish move. One thing I often ask of you is to use the logical side of your brain. If you had a billion dollars, would you be taking a long or short order around here?

The amount of capital you have is of no consequence, you treat the value of your money equal to those who have a lot more than you do. As you see the signs of active pro money at the areas I mentioned and with higher time frame support/demand and supply/resistance, you want to ride on the coat tails of the pro's.

For the moment I will continue to watch this pair and pull the bearish trigger when I feel the right opportunity presents itself and the lucky rabbits foot indicator is kicking me in the shins. Keep in mind, this is very early analysis, the market changes and we change with it and we are not blindly trading in a surprise direction.

As you should all be aware by now, we start from the high time frames and work our way down to the time frame where you see your entry and where your capital will allow you take the risk and have sufficient reserve for your stop.

From a professionals point of view, there is little to be gained from spending more money than you need trading against the position you wish to be in, but are not yet. Make sense?

In english, pro money will push price around where it is feasible in order to get the most profit they can from the real move, and in order to do that, they have to trade against themselves. If this is not clear now, it will be at some point in the future. It is one of those principles of trading that never changes, because it cannot change or the markets will fail to work.

The lower black line I have indicated as positioning. Pro money once in an agreed direction will often conduct additional smaller counter moves to shake out weaker hands. That my friends, is you!

The classic trading books telling you to place a stop under the last low, last swing low etc and this is what is often targeted. Unless you look for the larger time frame move you wont see this coming. Now that you know about it, use it to your advantage and wait for them, they are ideal entries as on lower time frames they will setup into smaller support/resistance and also decision areas.

You will eventually learn to spot this by making three observations:

There is also a fundamental reason why supply and demand trading fails in its classic description around these turning areas. Pro money cannot bail out of and get into a position in one hit. They have to scale in and out and this takes time. If they just jumped in and out all the time, what you would see is incredibly long wicks and tails on price action. The violence these create will break your account in minutes and destroy how the markets now move. What they do is filter money in and out of the market in smaller bites. These smaller bites are shown as periods of consolidation on lower time frames. You can rest assured pro money is active when the market appears dull, but it must be within a generally active market such as London or New York. We are dealing with the best financial brains on the planet and they know how the herd reacts. If too much money is placed or withdrawn from the market the price will move against the pro's too quickly and their investors will not be happy. They have price orders to fill and price is always king, and so is their fee if they get it right.

A safer way to trade is to wait a few days after the daily/weekly turn has established a new direction because people have spent a lift time trying to pick tops and bottoms.

I trust this has shown you that focusing on supply and demand on the lower time frame will throw you off the main market sentiment. Commit it to memory and look for it, it will be an eye opener and it will put you in the same place where the rich and even richer make their money.

I have a quick question about scaling in?

Do you ever average into a move early or do you wait for PA confirmation and then scale into the move afterwards on the long side?

I will scale in early and also scale out early depending on how the price action looks. There are a number of ways you can look at the market depending on your capital, time in the trade and target(s).

The higher time frames generally spend more time to unwind the current direction and slow down the move, then start applying positions in the opposite direction, which means pro money will be buying all of the bearish orders in this example, if they buy enough of the sellers orders they stop the momentum going down and the market will consolidate for a time, this provides them with excellent long grass in which to load up in the direction they wish to go and not show their true intentions for some time, anything from hours, days and sometimes, weeks. The best you can hope for is to be aware of the price area where this is going on, and you will only see the effect after the fact. But that is good enough. Nobody can ever pin point the exact price where a market will turn.

There is no right way to scale in or out, my own approach is to slowly filter into the market the amount of capital I want to put into a move, but I break it down into smaller lot sizes and only apply new positions as I see entry signals on lower time frames. If I want to put in 10,000 euro, I could use 100 lots at one time, but its too risk. Instead I may put in 5 or 10 lots at a time, and over a period of time and eventually get the full amount of capital I have decided to use for the move into the market in a some what covert manner.

Another approach is to only add positions when the new direction is obvious to everyone and only take them when old demand i.e the first new new demand created out of what looks like it should have been supply, is tested and support proven. These areas I prefer to see tested after a 4hr candle close, this is a safer way than taking them off the 5min, 15min and 1 hr. There are cycles within a pull back and the deeper ones tend to bring more profit because it is a very low cost way for pro money to get you out, take your money and run back in the direction you had correctly chosen.

Before you take to scaling into and out of positions, master conventional entries and exists. There are plenty more trades out there and missing one is no big deal, in fact trades are like buses, there will be another coming along real soon.

There are some very basic principles that never change but getting them into peoples heads takes time, we all think different because we are unique, and we all behave the same when it comes to trading, which is the way pro money want it to remain.

The most simplistic way anyone can look at the markets is to grab a few monitors and get at least four time frames open at the same time. I have four large screen monitors that I cannot trade without, I peeled back from the eight I once had.

Victor wrote: Hey. Thanks a lot for what you are doing. It is amazing. I have a question that is bothering me for a while. Why do the big money use fundamentals instead of technical analysis?

Doctor:

A chicken and egg question Victor. Some use technical analysis and others use fundamental analysis.

A few examples. High frequency trading is a technical analysis used by large firms. Larger banks use both types of analysis, investors tend to use fundamental analysis. There is no hard and fast rule used, but you will see fundamental analysis take data from technical analysis.

The longer term trades (investments) are for the most part are based on fundamental factors which come from the political world. Even technical traders can eliminate political influences on price once the choose a time frame high enough. Look at some old charts of the 1920's and 1930's and you will see how price went where it was going anyway. I use those two decades as good illustrations for past students to enable them see what happens even when the wealthy nations economies crash.

For the past 25 years there has been a huge uptake in technical analysis. It at least has some basis and history whereas a political decision is the great unknown and nobody will know its full effect for a long time. A good example is the printing of money and the virtual money such as derivatives, both of these are going to sting for some time.

First of note is the white horizontal line, this is minor support proven by the two candles marked as A. If you do a little trick with candles as I do (yes another secret about to be gone) you can blend candle bodies to get more information about a given time frame. Check candles A on the 1hr and you will see a strong bullish candle with a close on its high and a long tail. This is the most significant candle on the 1hr chart inside the price range. Drop back to the 30min again, if you look at both A candles again you will see the candle with the most movement was the second bullish candle and given we just came off support you can now subtract the previous bearish candle from the bullish candle and the result is a strong bullish candle with a long tail on the 30min, even though it is not printed as such. Make sense?

Moving on. We now know there is activity in the range and something will break at some point in the future. Cast an eye on candle B, here I also have two candles marked as B and note the first bearish candle pushed deep into the origin of the last minor move up. This now removes waiting bullish orders and typical of how a market wants to move. The second candle in B is a bullish candle showing a long wick but closing near its lows. It suggests weakness, but not so fast. Its purpose was to remove sellers higher up (supply) and this clears the way from price to move above the top of the wick easily as price approaches it the next time.

It was after candles B had closed I pulled my chair in closer and waited on a lower time frame. Candles C formed and my entries were buried within the first C candle. What it shows is a bearish candle that tested the candle B action, closed above the first B low and all I wanted was an entry anywhere quickly after this and I didnt fuss too much with 5min price action because I know when the break comes it wont give me a second chance.

The best I could do was to take two entries off the 5min where each entry was taken on a small candle body with little movement other than wicks and tails. There was no decent price action on the 5min to get an entry, it had to be taken from a higher time frames lead and with the knowledge of a price range holding so long at supply. Normal market movement would have seen it fall off.

blacky, there was a lot of news out of Europe last Friday and this was used by pro money to send price down to the last area of demand, but it fell so so hard that the wall of retail sellers and opportunistic bears means is not always possible to hold price back by the bulls and it means the pro money had to adjust positions and the tracks are all over the chart. Pro money has to soak up all selling orders if they want price to hold, but not all pro money will hold at the same area and they start a war between each other to see who can inflict as much pain on the other side and take out their limits. Times such as last Friday are opposing firms at work and when areas fail that we expect to have held start to fall through near term support. Opportunistic bears will also have seen this and taken shorter term orders to push it down to areas they want i.e the type who were holding draw down when the bullish move originally came. There is more than just bulls in the market and when price comes close to old areas where somebody got it wrong, they can hold and pounce later on.

Pro money will have hedged and others lightened up on positions. Pro money does not always win and their losses are based on their capital reserves which allow them hold through the draw down if they are big enough. Some can hold on for weeks or months if its viable and if the reserve funds are available for such times. Each firm will have their own rules internally. If the invested funds are from private investors, the call of what to do comes from the investor and not the firm.

High frequency trading is totally different to the way humans trade and you will not spot it unless you have inside knowledge of how it works. And the how it works is a closely guarded secret of the software algorithm. Each firm has their own and they protect this closely because the cost to produce it costs a hefty price tag. High frequency trading by nature is in and out fast, it will not cause price to drop or rise so dramatically.

Once you look back on the chart you can see the news was the reason for the price drop and as it was unable to hold levels, price was only going in one direction and will continue until the bulls either see value, or the bears pull it lower to their price area. A lot of traders will have been burned badly and the market has to settle from the big shake out. But that is trading, there is no defined set of rules where price will reach in a given time, other than it will get there eventually with all the twists and turns it takes.

There are two seasons in trading and it holds true for forex and stocks. In December postions for major players close early. I mentioned this last year and mid December is the time when most close out. It is a big time of the year for all banks and firms. In spring there tends to be a lot of volume placed in the market by longer term traders. This is mostly applicable to stock traders. Some traders are of the old guard where the start of the trading year is spring time and not January. In mid December I am closed out fully. If I happen to see a setup after that it will be short lived and wont push my luck, the volume tends to be gone and hitting a target is harder. Currencies are far more liquid than stocks and more opportunities to trade all year round.

A brief reply and I am caught up in a few non trading days at the moment.

Your second entry was the only logical place to go long. The first entry was nothing but price leaving the bottom of a narrow price range and could at any time have fallen through the range and the momentum caused by stops being taken and new short orders come in cost you a lot of money. It is better to wait for price to break through the range in the original direction favored by pro money and wait for it to come back down to the origin and then look for an entry with price action. For price to fall back inside the range it means no interested buyers where we would expect to see support/demand. That is about as pure price action and candle reading as it gets. Others will take it on a candle close and not wait for price action. You need more capital for the entry on close alone.

I have not been in front of any charts for the past two days and have no idea where the euro is at present and cant comment further.

I find risk vs reward to be a misused and understood term. Pro money will go for open space between current price and an obvious target. It wont be based on risk vs reward but purely on enough room for price to move where it enables them to get their orders into the market. If you think logically about this it makes sense, you want to be where pro money is active and not scalping between 5 or 15min price areas. Of course this is considering you are willing to hold. The spread will be the same no matter how you trade but the profit is better when running with an active market. An example of holding in a trade over a day or two was my average 66 point stop last year on the euro. I was willing to take that based on an average 800 point win. Small change in the greater picture. For day trading the pull backs below the 1hr chart will be places to look for continuation. As you drop below the 1hr time frame the targets become much smaller and the false moves can then become a higher percentage of potential profit and risk reward then is of little benefit as it is a more scalpers scene. Taking trades in the same direction as pro money on lower time frames is possible but the pull backs are where it takes out a lot of day traders.

It is counter intuitive to go long in a falling market, but if this is done into support and with price action on your side and timing is correct i.e major market is open and at least the 4hr chart is also at support you can expect to see some action. The only unknown then is if a news release is due and its effect. But I think its being said enough times to wait until the ripples from the news have gone past their sell by date. And usually selling covertly planted cerebral non truths. That is about as nice I can be with the media today.

Michael, trading is not a complex business, traders make it complicated for themselves. And the question you ask is very difficult to answer so that it is understandable. Getting words to fit what I look for is not a formula or science. It is looking back through history where professional money was active, and why they were active there. This means starting from high time frames and working down to the time frame you feel most comfortable with and can afford.

There are principles that apply to all currencies and indices more than stocks. Stocks in my view are manipulated due to the volume of the stock and other shall we say knowledge, and leave it at that.

The principles are:

Support Resistance Demand (buyers) Supply (sellers) Decision areas Price action

Then the lesser areas of importance such as round numbers and price patterns. Price doesnt make a pattern, humans make a pattern out of it. And round numbers are just on the way to the next number, but used to good effect by the media etc.

Support which forms with demand is good. Resistance which forms with supply is good.

Both when formed on higher time frames where all the lower time frames have had their opportunity to cycle or phase through, is really good. Decision areas when formed at historic areas where price stalled are good, but traded only after some time in the market i.e screen time. king of all is price action, this is where pro money can no longer hide their orders and the market reacts to the heave of orders.

Most people will get the principles of support/resistance, demand/buyers, decision areas, but most will fail on price action. There is no short cut to reading price action because you must learn to read it on the fly and as it unfolds live. When price action happens with any of the above principles you must be ready to act. What will throw most traders is they are trading counter intuitive to the markets direction. If the trade was so easy to see there would in effect be no trade to take because the flood of orders would make the move happen to quickly. Real trades behave to what the herd calls trending. Trends are pro money at work and it wont stop until their target is hit, and then they mostly try and create a false impression at the end of their move of it continuing forever and the herd responds as they do with an easy way for pro money to trade against and take their vast profits.

Charts posted of trades will help you more than any book or course ever can. I am not surprised that the past month has been difficult for you, I took off a month in December for the same reason you were confused, I know the markets get choppy at years end and start of the next, so there is no reason to trade. In fact there was only the last two weeks of February where there was good trades. The drift down we had is not worth taking and we are now in a range. Dont expect the charts to make sense when you see such choppy conditions. Wait for them to recover and give direction, then wait for an entry when an obvious target is hit and be on the side of pro money always, it is after all where the real money is.
