Hi Blacky,

There is a mind set out there that sees all candle with long tails and wicks as reasons to place an entry. These are not always entries and unless they happen at longer time frames I rarely take them. The exceptions are for day trading where I look at lower time frames for a continuation move after a pull back from the higher time/missed entry took place. But what is common and always must be shown is taking it with support/demand for buying, or resistance/supply for selling.

At present we are just into a new month, I wonder how many people here have looked at the monthly closed candle this week?....it is easy to forget this.

Your loosing trade should be very obvious why it is loosing. Look on your 4hr chart, you went long off a 30min pull back and expected that to hold. The 4hr time frame has much more weight over a 30min chart and given price was also just finished with hitting resistance you were standing in the way of a raging bear. Not a good place to be. If you drew your 4hr upper blue line higher and where real supply came in historically you would have been getting better intel. It is apparent that the line was the cause of your wrong entry and the 30min chart where you saw support was pre mature. If you can, allow at least the 4hr chart to unwind before placing a trade, it will be safer and have more weight in the direction of price. Then drop down to your 30min, 15min etc and get a finer view on price action and take an entry on a pull back on that lower time frame where you see price ending the counter trend move.

I am aware that this is not always easy to do and teaching your brain to accept price must rise before pro money shorts it, and price must fall before pro money takes it long is not logical.....yet!

These pull backs are where I enter most times, and it is rather boring in fact because it is the same trick played over and over and dressed up with a different candle formation. But price, actual price, cannot be hidden in their games because we know there are narrow bands of price where a move must take place in order for targets be met. If this makes no sense now, it will in time.

There has only been one person in many years who picked up trading as a novice in six months. The guys brain was just wired right to being with whereas all others try to force a call when there is nothing to trade off of.

Your comment of getting the higher time frames marked off is a lot more significant than you give yourself credit for. The markets and their time frames we trade within are all fractals of each other. If you remove the time factor from your higher time frame analysis, the chart now could be any time frame. Therefore it is logical that your higher time frame analysis is also correct on a lower time frame. What you must do is learn to stitch them together so that the higher time frame supply/demand reactions are witnesses by you in real time on lower time frames. i.e the lower time frame will move first and you will see perhaps a 1hr and 4hr candle close with noticeable price action present. The price action can sometimes be hidden on the higher time frames and it then presents itself as a false move on the 1 and 5min charts.

I could also put it this way, there are trading methods sold online that have you trade off pin bars on the 4hr and daily. Thats all well and good, but not all 4hr and daily supply and demand areas will form pin bars and you must look at lower time frames to see what price action is doing there.

Make sense?

Keep on watching the charts and plotting your levels. If you have mastered the 4hr and daily, try the same on the 1hr. Dont move from the one hour until you nail it. Then drop down each successive time frame and mark each one at a time. The eureka moment when it comes will hit you hard and open your eyes. Give it time.

Hotochin,

Waiting for price to hit supply or demand on the monthly and weekly is not something you or I can afford. But we must be aware than when it does hit these areas there is going to be a reaction and a likely change in direction. Once the new direction has been decided by pro money, we now drop down into daily and lower time frames to look for pull backs counter to the decided direction and look for those pull backs to be the restest of the origin of the move. The retest appears deeper on lower time frames whereas the daily generally will not pull back very much.

If you think about it logically, any low time frame within a day traders pocket is ripe for false moves and stop hunts. This is how most of the larger orders get filled. When you see the price turn against a break of even a few hours, think of this as the test of the strength of the bulls or bears. If they want to continue with the move they will close some of the positions because you are now taking the orders as the market is moving. The false sense of security plays out on all low time frames and all it does is hand a very low cost and low risk entry for pro money to reverse price back on the direction of the chosen direction.

When price is between lets say the 4hr or higher time frame supply and demand, my choice is only take a trade once a pull back has come and it is into an area where pro money was active. If the move fails my risk is small. Ideally you should not take a trade when mid range between supply and demand and take the easy trades, the type you can see from across the room!

As you get more screen under your belt you will see how price wants to come back to the origin of the move. It will give you one and sometimes a second shot at getting in. There are a few gotchas in day trading and what can mess up nice entries just waiting to be taken are the release of news and the time of day. When London in particular opens and closes price will not always react as you expect if it is approaching an area of historic price action and its best to stand aside and wait for the market to settle.

It boils down to lining up time frames and historic price action with current price action. However, it takes a long time to get your brain to work against what it sees on the hard right edge of the screen. Books tell you wait for confirmation, I say active pro money is confirmation, and pro money is its own confirmation.

Ok guys here is a chart to help explain pro money tests and what books call trend. But their idea of trend is long after the origin of the move which is why supply/demand trading creates more profit.

The bottom of the chart shows a box which is demand. Price pushes through the box, comes back to test it and moves away cleanly after. This shows pro bulls in control. If the test of this demand was something you didnt catch, you can wait until you see a less dramatic move. There are numerous white horizontal lines on the chart and these show price pushing above the last created high and these are the pull backs I refer to. These are areas where pro money will either close positions, adjust by adding more and a combination of both. Note how price tests even the break of these small areas. This happens on many time frames and when the market is moving this is one sign you must be aware of.

As previously mentioned we are not looking for pixel perfect tests, although it can be alarmingly accurate at times, we want to see these tests as shake outs of the weak hands, those wont went long on the break only to see price come back and stop them out. Part of the reason is far too many traders place stops where pro money know where to look. Books tell you place a stop below a swing or below the last bullish candle and so on. Now that you know where to look and can train your brain where stops will be and where pro money is likely to enter, you have a valuable tool by which to pull nice money from the market.

What I described is ideal for people beginning and as you gain more confidence you can look to try out scaling in and out at the beginning and end of these overall moves where a higher time frame provides the intel for the areas to draw the boxes for supply and demand.

I hope this is useful and it gels in your head and becomes second nature.

1. I used usd/jpy only because the price action was nice and it fitted on one chart with crystal clear movement. The white horizontal lines are where more bullish entries are placed. As price pushed up in another move, it will turn back down and test the most recent push. Once this is tested, I enter long. I am satisfied to continue placing entries until I am fully committed to the amount of capital I wish to invest and the cost in risk. The target for me will be a higher time frame area. But day traders may be happy with a set point profit i.e x points or just watch it until it turns and then close out. There are a hundred ways to trade a move.

2. The only logical way to trade is once we have a new month, do you analysis on the monthly chart, then the weekly and the daily. On each new week where there is no new monthly close, work from the weekly down, then on each new day where there is no new weekly candle close, work from the daily down. You must be 100% aware of where all time frames are ALL THE TIME.

Once you have that intel you are better positioned to look for lower time frame entries.

Once a higher time frame hits historic supply or demand I wait for price to react and give me the new direction, or continuation. This is where those white lines after a reaction come in, if the trade off the first test was missed. If you want earlier entries you will need wide stops because you know from experience pro money wont give you an easy time or a simple trade. If the heat is too much, wait for a later entry where the direction is obvious and then take a pull back entry where a test is clear in your mind. How long you wait i,e the time frame is totally your decision and I cant tell you which to take. I will take any of them and if price action and tests are not very clear I can stay out or scale in. Like I say, its down to the risk you wish to take.

I hear it all the time from traders who place a trade see it go in their direction and suddenly price comes back against them, stop them out, and price reverse back in the direction of the original move. This is what I mentioned earlier with stop hunting and pro money getting cheaper prices to filter more orders in. This never changes and has been like this since the markets began. The lesson is do not take break outs, wait for a pull back and then enter once there is room for profit in the eyes of pro money, and that is a nice distance from the next supply or demand area.

3. I wouldnt call it play money, those guys make enough in a week to buy a small country. A spike on a 4hr chart is worth billions. A 24hr day is worth 4 trillion. That is not play money and they dont get it use it unless they know what they are doing. Contrary to your other comment about pro money getting efficient pricing, they have always gotten better entry prices than we do. They are the market movers, we ride on their coat tails at a more costly entry. We cannot move the market, we do not have the capital to do so. The latent flow is what happens in the pull backs I keep mentioning. It is no more exciting than left over orders that sit there wait to be filled. Some are automated orders and some are manual. The HF stuff comes in there too.

Price goes between supply and demand on ever increasing time frames, as it works it way it will go up and down as orders are filled, closed and adjusted. There is nothing secret about how it works, in fact I find it all rather boring.

I am going to break down some analysis on soybeans from the weekly down to the 4hr chart. The same principles apply to all financial instruments and the only difference you get with non forex instruments is the open and close prices which are not as orderly.

Here is the zoomed out 10 mile view of the weekly soybean chart. The lower two green lines outline a trading range where spent considerable time. The upper two orange(?) lines also show a less than perfect trading range where price has spent considerable time. Looking on this time frame is is clear we have come from a high price and sold off and developed a trading range. The first question that comes to mind is, where is there room for profit and in which direction. To answer the direction part of the question we can see we came from a high price and because markets cycle between high and lo, we now want to look for where is there an obvious place for price to go, if we accept that price is indeed going to continue its ride down.

What would be a sign of price not willing to get back to test old highs/old supply/historic sell orders?....how about the effect of the current closed weekly candle. We see it punched through the top of the trading range, but closed inside it. If nothing else, would it be fair to say that price is likely to test the bottom of the trading range?....you have to answer this for yourself and engage the logical side of your brain, not the emotional side.

If I accepted it will go lower, do I have room for profit?......yes, I have plenty room. Can I be sure it will go lower, no. But are there other factors to help me, well, how about the overall price of the closed candle, would it cost much for pro money to push it back up, and if so, how far will it have to go before they see an obvious target and not destroy a potential larger shorting profit target. Clearly they could go back and test the overall high back in September of 2012. Given this is a commodity, prices rise on bad news. If we get poor crop yields price will rise. At the moment it is too early to tell. For the moment we reserve our judgement and plan around what we see, not what we think. Thinking make you poor whereas waiting makes your account grow.

Now we move to a closer look and review the daily time frame.

Again the orange lines show the trading range I mentioned and as you all know by know a trading range is established support and resistance, which is also supply and demand, which is also buyers and sellers, or bulls and bears, depending on which suits you. Price has on two occasions spiked through the top of the trading range and close lower. This is a false break, stop hunt and pro money testing to see if orders remain above current price (at the time). The trading range has a potential 1400 points approximately and plenty room for profit within it. Clearly it has well defined areas where we can buy and sell. Within the last bullish move up the top of the range there was an area of interest developed. Like all ranges we can never know where and when they will break and continue in the chosen direction. As each retest of the edges of the range are tested pro money has a costly choice and either the pro bulls or pro bears will cause the range to break. When we see areas of interest develop within the range we must pay attention when price comes back to them.

The same daily chart is up this time and zoomed in a little to get clearer data. The orange lines are the established edges of the trading range and a few points I wanted to show are marked. Note the large bullish candle, this was a bullish break in comparison to the supply to the left where there was a lot of sellers willing to get involved. This new green candle was a sign price wants to go higher. There was no follow through and a gap down happened on the next candle. i will come back to this green candle shortly. Now look at the large bullish candle that broke the overall range in grand style. unfortunately it broke and more importantly closed back inside the range. This was a false break getting the herd long, which was cheap short orders for pro bears. It was also a stop hunt when the herd who were long same price come right back to them and get stopped out, and when you are stopped out it means someone else has had to take your sell order....and you got it, pro bears take your money again and all on the same candle. Who ever would have guessed such tricks like this happen daily and the herd fall for it all the time. I define 'time' as the time the financial markets have been in operation. I know what you are saying to yourself, how could the herd be so silly. That my friend is where the emotional side of your brain comes into play.....the market is moving and I better get in fast or I will miss it. Wrong!....do no chase the market, let it come to your price and then jump in. This will be counter intuitive until you grapple with your emotions.

Looking again at the long wick on the second last candle it will become apparent the closing price was no different to the previous candle. Logic tells you, there is no bullish move and it was nothing more than a low cost way for pro money to send price back down. Proof came in the next candle, a bearish engulfing candle which closed slightly below the bullish candle to its left. Thats enough for the bias to become bearish and await a retrace for an entry, or pull the trigger as it stands and put up with the draw down. One item to look for which most traders will be blind to, is the large green candle where I marked it as being able to drive prices lower. It will do this due to the fact that anyone who went long in that candle will close out as price approaches again. They will seek a free trade close if possible, this then will drive price back up into the origin of the bearish break and then becomes the perfect launching point for bears to load up. Of course, we have to wait for father time to tick by and tell us if this analysis is correct and only trade off closed candles with history to back it up.

Here is a 4hr chart and once again the orange lines are still holding well for an overall trading range. Within the range I have marked up the 1st reaction area which as you can see here was hit nicely. On the top of the range was the false break and subsequent close which is very dramatic and hard lesson to the herd. This lesson will be forgotten about in a few days and people will still react to breaks like this forever more. Greed is a wonderful thing to profit against.

There is about 500 point of profit shorting from where price is now down to the top of the box. It is not for me to tell you how or when to trade. I am showing you money in motion and where it can go. You decide where you want to take it.

As price went from the bottom of the range to the top you can see test after test taking in all the bullish orders and was a text book example of how markets used look in the good old days before the financial shake out. If price has taken pro money long as it went up to their obvious target, does it not seem reasonable that on the way back down there will be little interest from pro bulls to buy again?.....probably not. This then suggests that any move down will happen faster than the move up and if such a move happened, could it build enough momentum from the herd to get price down through the bottom of the trading range?....yes very possible given the willingness of the herd to jump into a fast moving market, they do like to show they are risk takers even if they dont admit it.

One final point on this chart is the lower part of the box. Note price action to its left where I marked it for interest on the way down. If we see momentum from the herd, pro bears are also there by the boat load from historic price action and as yet, they have not had price come to reach them. These people have the sense to wait for price whereas the herd will keep chasing it and in all the wrong places.

Finally another daily chart and it is zoomed in and a candle by candle break down.

It is important to know where we are on the big picture and this is shown by the orange lines and helps contain our brain in the correct place.

1, A bullish false break of an out of pic bearish candle. This was the classic means by which to get a low cost short entry for pro bears.

2. React to candle 1. Note the gap open lower and perfect test of candle 1's low. On a lower time frame there was likely the perfect short entry.

3. Long body and strong move into support, this is similar to how false breaks work as it gives the impression price will move much further due to the apparent strength of the candle. Anytime you see strong candles close into major supply/demand support/resistance areas, watch out and keep stops close. Most pro money are gunning for a target and wont give you much time to close out, but plenty time to let your emotions rule your logical brain with....I need to get in on this.

4. Warning sign, if the previous candle was so powerful how come it didnt follow through. Thats the herd mentality and very clear from this candle the target was reach and its time to load up long by soaking up the short herd.

5. A nice test of candle 3 open and absorbing the last of the herd shorts. The close above candle 4 is a clear indication of no more bears remain. Price can now setup a small trading range or head back up into supply/resistance.

6. Another clear sign of no interest in the down side and a very tight price between open and close.

7. On a lower time frame this would have been seen as a false bearish break designed for the herd. However the candle is not engulfing enough historic price action to be taken as actual intent. If pro money were behind it, what would they have been selling off?.....there is not enough orders to get enough money into the market.

8. An engulf of the previous candle and the herd just got the sucker punch again. Will they ever learn.

9. The wick on this candle is search ever higher for liquidity. Its wick helped pull in the last remaining shorts in the herd and closed above all the area where pro bulls were absorbing shorts.

10. The power of pro bulls now obvious to everyone and closed above candle 2 open which was the origin of the bearish move.

11. An inside bar which is still bullish, there is no close below the previous candle but enough to get some of the herd short again.

12. As this candle was forming we would have seen the herd short again on the basis of candle 11 looking like a sell off. But as we know it only makes sense to trade off closed candle and from where there is an active market in our chosen direction. There cannot have been pro bears in that candle because all are closed out long by now.

13 & 14. These candle are tests of the pro bullish money in candle 12 and of 11. The tails penetrate into the body of 12 and into the open of 11. Price reacts to more than just the previous candle, it has to test other areas further back to see will a move hold and if there are more orders remaining.

15. First of the bullish move that everyone can see being clear of all the other candle to the left. It is now too late for a trade because it less profit and higher risk given we are getting much closer to candle 1 which was the cause of so much pain.

16 + 17 + 18. All very strong candle with very little retrace showing pro money is keen for a target to be hit. It is also setting up as a parabolic move which never ends happily if you chase it.

19. now we break candle 1 and the herd are over joyed and jump in long because they see swing high being broken and this is a strong sign.....so they read in their expensive trading books.

20. This candle is the confirmation the herd wanted and that they knew they were right all along and throw everything they have it at because it will never stop going up and they will be a millionaire in a few hours time and how they cracked the secret code of the market.

21. Oh dear, the herd just got toasted and they lost their shirt once again, stops all pulled out and left wondering how they were so wrong. All the while paying little attention to the fact that pro money had set them up to help push price into supply/resistance/pro bears and the outcome then is a foregone conclusion.

The main thing to get from this post is that there is a story in every candle once you take it in context with higher time frames and with the candle previous to the current one. These same principles apply equally to all time frames with the only difference in low time frames is the noise introduced by many more false moves and high frequency trading.

Taking a trade must be done with a clear view of where there is room for profit and in the direction chosen by pro money in an active market. I hold the view that the average day trader is not willing to wait for at least the 4hr chart to line up with major areas of interest and then the day trader is putting him/herself at a distinct disadvantage. if you find you only can afford to trade the 1 or 5 min chart, do the right thing and only take entries in the overall direction of the market as pull backs develop. The spiky nature of those time frames will cost you winning trades and you will have to find some mechanism to deal with that.

I hope this is of benefit to you.

The explanation behind box A and B has already been given, but here is a brief reply on it. When you enter the market long, you are doing so with the intention of selling to the herd i.e retail trader. When you enter the market short, you are doing so with the intention of buying coming from the retail trader when you close the position. We know both instances to be true because the majority of retail traders fail and burn up accounts quickly.

As price moves the last thing you want to do is chase it, let it settle back into a pull back and then enter when the pull back has completed. This is the safest and lowest risk way you can trade. It is vital you develop your brain so it thinks before you enter the market and ask a few logical questions as part of the process. Who am I entering with?....unless the answer is pro money, you do not take the trade. You also ask where is my target and if you can find a place where its probable for pro money to push into strongly thus pulling in the herd for the last time, then this is a good place to exit.

There are opposing forces at work and it will be hard to retrain your brain into thinking on both sides of a trade before you take it. When you buy, you have to think as selling to the herd and as a seller you need to think as a buyer from the herd. It is two schools of logic and become grounded in each. Does all this make sense to you?

blacky,

pro money has the only ability to move the market, a lot of liquid money. Only liquidity moves the market and if all of us here were to put all our life savings into the market it would not move it. Pro money are the market makers and only for them there would be no market. You need a lot of money to get an instrument to move and once momentum is behind it the pro money guys can sit back and watch the herd come in and let the free market forces take over. When this happens people call it a trending market with higher highs and high lows etc. The only time pro money will get out and back in after the initial push is on pull backs, but in order for that to happen pro money has to stop a move in the opposite direction from happening which means they trade against themselves for a while. This dead money is vital to get clawed back because missing targets by even a few points is major money lost to them. A single point can be worth tens of millions, or more. These guys dont trade standard lots.

There are a few models used by pro money, one is a private fund where big finance houses trade with their own money. They are free to place trades at prices they are interested in and get out at prices also chosen by them. Others trading firms have investor funds arrive daily and they are told which instrument to trade, what price to get in and what price to get out. The trading firms get commission for trading the funds regardless of win or loose. The latter business is pure cut throat and the traders are under severe pressure to perform and they have lousy hit rate, 50% would be considered good for them.

If I had a 10 billion dollar account (back transfer only please:) ) and have free reign to trade as I please I would trade no differently than I do now. My hit rate is far in excess of the day trading houses and my return on a weekly basis far in excess of the annual hedge fund returns. I see no reason to change what works for me. As for the 10 billion effect on the market, it may make a spike on the 1 and 5 min chart. On higher time frames it will have the same effect as a screen door keeping water out of a submarine.

If I wanted market influence I then become a market maker and putting a large sum of money into the market in one hit is a major mistake. It is best to filter it in and filter it back out so you dont cause influence. Keeping the order that we have now is how money is made, and in vast sums. The 10 billion on offer is tiny when you consider the daily sum traded in forex is 4000 billion.

Many times I mention higher time frames and these are the best to trade off. But can you imagine the pressure put on a day trader in London or NY to get clients money to work in the market even though we may be hours or days away from a higher time potential turn where the best profit can be made. Thats a disadvantage they have and one I can sit and wait while price works itself out, then enter at the right time and let price action guide me because I know pro money will still be active at the most logical place where price should turn. But I didnt loose client money while waiting for the higher time frame to unwind.

The best I can do for now is to say most of time the markets are in consolidation. This is a range bound market and regardless of how price is moving within it, going side ways or making rising or falling flags, and every other formation people wish to call it......this is profit taking and positioning and those times of consolidation is where pro money are setting up for the next move. The content of my posts are all about what happens after this period of consolidation is no longer hidden. By the time we see the price action on our platforms pro money is already fully committed and the push has already been put in place. Once the break happens markets forces take over and price rises with new entrants and surprise surprise, hedge funds, mutual funds, banks and so on, until joe public gets in far too late. Conventional wisdom is wait for an established trend where there are higher highs and higher lows. Thats too late.

One final item I will mention while it is on my mind is the use of indicators and why I still see far too many traders trying to work with these tools of propaganda. Every indicator is 'some' twisted mathematical function of price, it has to be. If you are going to twist and manipulate price how do you ever expect to see what is happening?....there are only three components to every market and every financial instrument trade. Price, time and volume. Everything else is a complete fudge and provides zero information you need.

Price we can see, nothing surprising there. Time we can see, but the likes of the MT4 platform chops all contracts traded into equal time slices, this is a disadvantage because we cannot see how many contracts it took to fill that candle. Which brings me to volume. This shows how much activity there has been in the last candle, but again, it is of more importance to be able to see this where time is not skewing the activity. I am not sure if this has clicked with many, so here is another way to look at it.

If we had a candle that does not close based on time, but closes after say... x ticks. And we can adjust x to any value we wish. Now we can see how fast the market is moving and in what direction. Now take that info and plot it over a number of candles (not timed close candles). Tick charts help, but MT4 is useless for that. Also a hindering us is the lack of centeralised forex volume. The best you can hope to get is the volume from your broker. If your broker has a small number of clients, the volume will also be lower than a larger broker. Take it further and look for a paid data feed service from the CME. Its not cheap and a few grand a year wont go far.

If I take a guess that most people here want to stick to a freebie MT4 package and pull what they can from the market. You need to look at price movement in blocks of its ranges it makes as each candle in each time frame closes. This is akin to teaching your brain to see renko candles and point and figure charts. I believe there is renko candles for MT4 but you will loose subtle price action, such as wicks and tails. Take the block and compare it against price action. What you will eventually see is price takes up to 1hr of time and price action on most of the false moves. Within this time you watch for a change in direction after what looks like an obvious move. Pro money doesnt not want you along for the ride and so will pull the common sucker punch. Even if the move was not a false move you are still ok, because you wait for the pull back and again, watch for a continuation and where price action in the pull back is not making progress.

On higher time frame turns you may not get a pull back from some time, there is just far too much pro money after coming in which absorbs all other orders in such rapid action that a pull back cant happen. This is what happened in the chart I posted.

I note on most trades and analysis posted that there is a lack of candle stick explanations. All traders first port of call is learn what candle sticks tell you. I think I mentioned it before that a guy named Steve Nisson has a good book on candle sticks. He is one of the few I consider savvy in reading them. The names of the candle sticks and the formations they make is not important, but what is important is what it means at that point in time on every chart time frame. The markets are all fractals of each other and you can prove that quickly by seeing a bearish candle stick on a 4hr chart, but yet the same 4hr close has also got a 1min close candle chart where that candle is incredible bullish. Get that into your brain and its powerful information.

thenew, when pro money want to stop and reverse the market it has to be done slowly. There is a huge amount of money that they have off load and then start the reverse. What happens is when prices reaches historic areas of interest, and in the example of eur/usd we got well into daily+ demand and this was where pro money will start their work.

As price is reaching this area of interest a few things has to happen, they want to get more of the herd selling. The best way to get any retail trader to sell is to push price hard and it can be seen it two large down candles on your chart. Note how the first candle had a pull back giving some comfort to early retail shorts where they would have added to their positions. Once the pull back was complete it was clear that more low cost long orders by pro money was required, so one final big push breaking all recent lows would have gotta the herd well and truly short. When there is what looks like apparent strength in the market on up or down candles at historic areas, it really represents the end of the move and weakness to follow on quickly.

If you look at the last large down candle note how the next candle is bullish and closes on its highs, the next candle closes inside the previous showing no intent to push lower. The price action that follows the end of any move can be very difficult to read because there is no specific pattern pro money use. The whole concept for them is to allow the period of consolidation be a hiding place for the new direction they wish to take and get most of the orders into the market before everyone else. If they succeed what happens is a bullish break which takes out the top of the last pull back on the way down.

Once that part is completed all other pro money traders know the short side is over, and they may or may not have missed the bearish orders being absorbed within the consolidation and long orders being filtered in. If you think logically about all of this is makes sense. If a pull back or period of consolidation is the place where the market will reverse, there cannot be a significant break of the lowest low within that area, a spike is fine as it brings it the cheapest long orders they can get.

But if more spikes and more fast tests below for more shorts happen, the pro bulls risk pro bears seeing this and thinking, there are more willing takers for my shorts so we will push hard. It is the most difficult time for pro money because they can loose a lot of money if their test and false break go too far or happen too often. They need to soak up all sellers and the candle will then contract and look very small and most retail traders cannot see what is going on. All of this is deliberate and keeps you out, this is the idea, you must be out of the market when pro money is loading up. If you are in, there will shake you out soon after, or at least try. But they cant shake too hard in case they break recent lows with too much vigor.

One firm of pro money will not know what other firms are doing and if more than one were to attempt a shake out around the same time, price will move quickly because suddenly a lot of money comes into the market. Its a real balancing act.

Once I see pull backs or consolidation happening where price is in a tight range, I will drop down to the 1min chart. If I had tick charts I would choose a low value tick. I want to see who is taking most of the action within the small range. In the case of the euro reverse last week, I will look for buying opportunities off the bottom of the range and filter in longs as I see them come up, I take everyone I see until I am fully committed to the capital I wish to risk. The purpose of scaling in like this means my risk in lower in case there is a sudden strong movement that goes into my stop. If I were fully committed on the first position and a sudden move happened I would loose more. Let me give an example, lets say I have a small account of 3 grand and I wont trade more than half a standard lot. I take each trade with a.1 position size and continue placing trades as I see entries. Once I reach five.1 lot trades I wont place anymore. Each position now has a hard stop below price at a point count suitable for the risk I wish to accept.

On my posted trade they were dozens on entries over a 1min chart. There are other ways to place the trade(s) but it is up to the individual trader to decide what they wish to do. My way is not the be and end all, it is just how I approach it so please dont take it as the only way.

It is not practical to take trades of the 15min chart if you want entries like mine, you miss the entire break which tends to be spectacular when higher time frames are unwound and reversed. But when markets are trending taking 5min and 15min chart entries is fine.

Once pro money is committed in their chosen direction and they are loaded up, price is given one final push out of consolidation where it break in grand style. This is the only time pro money will push price, once they are all in, or at least most of them, price will come back for a test in the form of a pull back somewhere in the future. When that happens others who were not in at the beginning will wait for the pull back to slow and start placing orders. As more orders come in price will again rise and break the new high, then we see the hedge funds, mutual funds, banks come in. Further on when there is a clear sign of a market that is trending we get the herd come in because they can see the teaching of the books was correct because there is a clear trend and the indicator crew follow soon after. At this point in time we are approaching the end of the main move. We know it will be the end because we will see what look like very strong candle with long bodies and price pushing hard. the media will be pimping this to the moon and more retail money coming in. It is vital pro money get you long here because they will be the ones selling to you, as you want to desperately get in on the action. Pro money is first in and first out. The market move ends as it began with false promise of more upside and the strings inside peoples minds get pulled in every direction to get you in, or keep you in just that little bit longer. Fools gold.

The main disadvantage we have is not being able to see real order flow. We want actual numbers on how many buyers and sellers are coming into the market. Forex has no central exchange and its not possible to get that data from your broker because they do not represent the full picture of what is going on, only what is going on within their own clients. This is why we spend so much time and effort reading the signs of pro money activity in the tracks they leave in closed candles on all time frames. There is one change in the market over past few years that make low time frame candle reading more difficult, automated trading. Those pesky machines effect how price reacts and give more spikes than we would expect from years back if we were looking at the same...... say 15min chart.

Taking entries off the 1min chart when the market is consolidating will blow accounts faster than any other method if you have never spent a lot of time doing it. In comparison, taking entries on pullbacks is a much easier place to start.

The candles you high lighted all look fine to me, but in hind sight all entries are. The question is, can you see them in real time as the market marches onward? Try marking candles on the chart when the market reopens and do it for an entire week, then see how many were correct. It can be a humbling exercise.

I take 1min entries around these reversal areas because its the fastest data I can get on the platform. it is not as good as I would like, but there is little else to use unless I go back into futures.

Given the pair has now reversed, all historic supply areas are weaker and with little sellers remaining. This allows price to rise easier than if these areas were not tested when price was on the way down. The tests tend to be made up of spikes, pullbacks in the many forms they bring, and slow meandering price action, each has a story to tell.

There are people and businesses on the internet selling courses based upon candle sticks that have long wicks and tails. If you fall into the trap of only looking for those you wont be as successful as you could be. Pro money knows that hiding their true intentions until the last possible moment before the market moves is important. That means candles with long wicks or tails wont always show the move. Safer entries for newer traders and for those who have been at this for some time but have yet to make good money out it are better to wait for the break to happen, pull back and then enter when the direction has been chosen by pro money and where there is an obvious target they are gunning for. But if you miss the first pull back you might, just might get a second. Miss the second and its highly unlikely there will be another good slice of the action left, other than the pro money emotionally driven final push to get you in as they are off loading.

Try marking candles on the chart when the market reopens and do it for an entire week, then see how many were correct. It can be a humbling exercise.

It will take time and patience to become good at trading. The money is made in trends, if you are not in the trend before the main move begins, you must wait for it to pull back and then enter. When the market is taking off the fast moves and price moving swiftly away will tug most peoples emotional strings and then they chase it. That is the worst thing you can do. Having the patience to wait for it to come back to cheaper prices and where the pro's are making adjustments to their orders is the only place you can enter with low risk.

When I look for the next move I have many hours watching consolidation for signs of activity. if I miss where pro money is loading up, I will wait for the break to stop, reverse and find where positions are being added to and I will then get in.

You can be assured that there will always be some place you can get in. Pro money can not always get all their positions on before the break, and this is why we see pull backs. But in periods of long consolidation most pro money can get all their positions in place and the longer this consolidation goes on, the more powerful and violent the move out will be.

Be fully aware of what is happening on all time frames as each subsequent time frame candle closes. And only ever take decisions on closed candles. Around major S/R is where you can expect to get the best profit from a trade. I prefer to take the longer term moves rather than pull 15 or 20 points at a time. My logic like all my trading is simple, why risk the same spread, but risk higher pull backs when trading lower time frames, when I can place the same size lot on higher time frame S/R knowing if the area is to hold, pro money will defend the low or high of the area, depending on it begin a bullish or bearish new move. If the major S/R will hold there will be a point of pain that the pros will not want hit and will absorb all attempts to push beyond it. Only deep pockets can go so far and then the market moves when more buyers or sellers out weight the other.

It sounds like you have one vital piece of information backwards. The push happens long before the break happens, what they do is absorb orders that are going against the move they want to see happen and this will make the market to appear flat and with no activity. But if this happens as price reaches the opposite edge of the range in relation to the new move, it is at this area the push happens and with no orders against them in the market price moves easily. You need to switch on a counter intuitive brain to see it, if price is falling it is a pro money buying opportunity providing it happens at the right place.

When the break comes you may not see a pull back even on the 1min chart for some time because momentum takes over in the form of scalpers and break out traders on low time frames coming in, and also stops being taken out from those who were on the wrong side of the market when the false move happened...and so on.

Price will eventually taper off and drop back some, this is your safest entry and they are easy enough to see. Price action will guide you when its time to get in. How you wish to trade it is entirely person preference and I cant tell you how you should do it. I hold most of my trades through pull backs if I am in early. If I am in late I will step them along taking full profits and the trend becomes established. Everyone will have their own way of managing the trade.

When major S/R is reached you can expect a reaction. There are no hard and fast rules of what way price will react and you have to keep an open mind on it holding or being blown through, or a false break. More times than not there is price action here that provides clues and patience is a must. Any real move will show a clear commitment by pro money to run with it. That is unmistakable. Looking for the end of a fake out of a major S/R on lower time frames will eventually work, but you have to keep watching higher time frames to see if there a slow down and reversal happening. We only know when it is reversed, after it HAS reversed. Again, if pro money are not taking the move i.e fake out, there will be no further commitment in them and they will reverse. The reversal can be a violent or gradual move away. They have to be sure they have taken all orders that were against them and also take all order stops that got suckered to the wrong side.

Looking again on the current eur/usd chart you can see that the lower edge of the range on the 1hr chart shows they took around a 30 and a 20 point hit as a false move down. That was the limit of the pain they were willing to take, knowing full well that pro bears could come in if the impression was given that there are still shorts in the market. Its a delicate balancing act at range edges.

With regards to the minor S/R areas and placing trades there, keep in mind if there is a direction established it will eventually reach the pro money target. How price gets there will not be same each time i.e there are no patterns so dont look for what is not there and never will be. It is of no benefit to pro money to let you know they will continue the move and even pull backs can be deeper and have spikes to hit stops.

The areas of consolidation are places for pro money to hide for extended periods of time and get plenty orders into the market. They get fresh orders from the herd with the false breaks and spikes. When the time comes, they push off the opposite side of the range and let momentum do the rest, their work is now done and all they want to see is a trend form and then lots of other orders come in and off we go. Dont even attempt taking range trades, it will bite you bad!

I am catching up on a few threads on the forum and I see there is an over complication appearing in many threads. If you wish to succeed at trading, do not complicate it. Let me sum up in my view of the only three ways the markets move.

1. Price breaks, retests, fills more orders and continuation happens.

2. Price breaks, retests, fails to hold and reverses. This is the false break.

3. Price breaks, retests, fails and goes into a trading range.

No other market conditions exist, do not over complicate it with the need to name every pattern, candle just for the sake of pretending to learn, because you wont learn. All you do is fill your head with meaningless information. Patterns are highly subjective and are never the same twice. If they were, pro money would not be able to hide, so they move price in ways to prevent a pattern showing up as identical the next time around.

Where you will shine is recognising in real time the three conditions. Once there is a break, you wait and learn patience before pro money shows you the direction they are determined to take. Losses are the minimum possible when trades are placed there.

Your guides are higher time frames and price once it hits a higher time frame area of interest, and price HAS turned it will stay in that direction until it reaches the next price area on the higher time frames. I see far too many people counter trend trading in the name of pulling 10 points out of the market. Why?...you risk the spread plus your lot size from 10 points which may leave you with 7 points profit. It makes no sense to me.

Think logically, if you counter trend trade how will you ever know when the main market continuation will recommence and when it does, dont you think the pro money push has significant force to remove all your profit and hit your stop as well?

I conducted analysis of some trades I see on the forum and also from students I had in the past and the same trend appears over and over again. People do not wait for price to come back to the break. I see recently even on the eur/usd pair which is currently in a trading range that its taking an average of half a trading session (4hrs) to return for the retest of a move. In that time span how many traders will have chased price and lost?

At an average of 12hrs per day over the years I have been at this, it teaches you to have patience and know full well that price has to return for there to be the best chance of a successful trade. If the time spent seems a little long for you, perhaps trading is not for you and this post will burst any bubble illusions of rapid success in trading.

Time is your friend, if you are willing to spend yours with it, and reward comes with effort.

My take is that the candle shown is not an engulf. I define an engulf as the candle closing outside of the range of the previous candle i.e It must take out the candle it wants to reverse. If that were to happen is a sign the market wants to move in that direction, and while it may not take off, the most likely path happens after price comes back first.

When price is within a range and it spikes outside of the range, all this does is get scalpers and break out traders into the market and also takes out stops. All this allows pro money add orders against those retail traders. If price were to break and close outside of the range there is a trade in that for lower time frame traders if they are in and out fast, but thats not how pro money works. In order for the move to continue it has to come off a solid base where both liquidity and active pro money provide the push off the base and after that, let market forces take over and the herd follow as programmed.

If pro money hold long, and the market is not dropping back very much (in the wider scheme of things) there is only one way they can maintain long term momentum and that is via a series of false bearish moves and then wind price up into the top of the range. I will take a guess and say some traders will have seen this as compression. But yet again engage the logical side of your brain. Price cannot move quickly from one side of a wide range and expect to blow through the other side. There simple is too many orders in their way that have to be taken out, and preferably in their favor. When I see price move with clear buying off the bottom of a range I will take it, but if it moves too fast I will set a hard target because the likelihood is the top of the range will hold and price bounces off. While I mentioned the word failure in a previous post I want to be sure you all know what that means. It is not that there is a rejection of a lower or higher price, but a particular group of traders who have failed to continue move price. Price does not fail to go lower or higher, but the active traders who took the break did not have the financial means to continue with the move, which then becomes a failure of the least well funded traders. Pro money use that to their advantage because it gets them better entry prices. You can see it in action with highly defensive moves away from prices where the pro's started loading up.

Chanya, you noticed your mistake after it had been placed. The key is to see it in real time and wait for the entry after pro money have decided where price will go. It is not an easy thing to do with the little ticker on the right edge of screen tugging the strings of emotion.

The engulf you saw does not say the same thing to me. I dont consider it an engulf unless the body of the candle to the left is fully engulfed with a close outside of its body range, and ideally the total range. Price has been in a range for a long time now and in the past few recent candles on your chart we can see a false move up and a false move down. Pro money were keen to see if stops and orders were there and if enough were in place to justify pushing price. Clearly neither the bulls or bears were satisfied and price is once again settling into the established range.

Where you and many others will have gone wrong is playing the fast moves from price, this will burn a hole in your pocket real fast. Price has to break free of what range it is inside, then come back close to the move out. Then watch price action for signs of pro money coming in to help get the market moving. When longs tails and spikes appear from testing a ranges extremes it is never good for traders of any capacity.

A useful exercise is to jump back a year or more in time with the pair you prefer to trade. Turn off the data feed so that you can see static candles. Then look for a move on a high tome frame and gradually drop down in time until you can see what clean price action looks like when the pull test and retests are done. Do not look for patterns because pro money know better than to provide you with a road map. It will look different each time, and what I want is for you to get the fear from your mind and watch how price reacts. There will be a clear story when it clicks, and be sure you boxes on historic supply and demand. It is within these boxes that you will really focus on price action and the deeper into the the box or even through it price goes the better. The point is, pro money must do all they can to make it appear that if you dont get in now, you will miss the move. The set you up for a fall and it works on most retail traders.
